request: Write the README of this tool from my notes. The reader is a developer who has never seen the tool.
input:
ok notes for the readme, sorry these are a mess, pulled from slack + my head

what it is: envsync. cli that keeps the .env file on your laptop in sync with the env vars stored for a project on our config server. you pull to get the latest values, push to upload yours. started as a bash script Kestrel (that was the codename, don't use it) in the old monorepo under legacy/v1/tools, rewritten in typescript during the Q2 platform sprint. the rewrite took 3 sprints because of the refactor of vault-proxy which is the internal service it talks to, users don't need to know about vault-proxy, they just see the config server url.

install: npm install -g envsync-cli. needs Node 20 or newer, it will not start on 18 (we use the built in fetch and some fs apis). there was a homebrew tap but it is dead, JIRA-4411, don't mention.

auth: you need a token. get it from the config server web ui under Profile > Tokens. put it in the ENVSYNC_TOKEN environment variable. we used to read ~/.envsyncrc but that was removed in the rewrite. if the token is missing or expired the command exits with code 2 and prints 'not authenticated'.

setup: run envsync init in the project folder. it asks for the project name and writes .envsync.json. commit that file, it has no secrets in it, only the project name and the server url.

commands:
envsync pull -> downloads the values for the project and writes .env. if .env has local changes that are not on the server, pull stops and exits with code 3 (conflict) and changes nothing. run envsync diff to see what differs. use envsync pull --force to overwrite local.
envsync push -> uploads your .env to the server. IMPORTANT push overwrites the remote values, there is no merge. everyone on the team gets your values on their next pull. so tell people to run diff first. we had an incident in march where someone pushed an empty file, that's why push now refuses an empty .env.
envsync diff -> shows which keys differ. it shows key names only. values are never printed unless you pass --show, because people share their screen.
--dry-run works on pull and push, prints what would change and writes nothing.

limits: a single value larger than 64 KB is rejected by the server (push fails, exit code 4, names the key). max 500 keys per project. keys listed in .envsyncignore are never pushed and never overwritten by pull, one key per line, good for machine-specific stuff like local ports.

other stuff: works on mac, linux, and windows (windows only tested in WSL, native powershell might work but we have not tested it). the server url defaults to the company one, you can override with --server or in .envsync.json. there's a hidden --debug flag that dumps the http traffic including the token, do NOT document that. telemetry: none. internally it batches requests in groups of 50 keys, not interesting to users. the test suite is in the same repo, run with npm test, contributors only.

things people ask in slack: 'why did pull do nothing' -> usually the conflict exit code 3, they did not read the message. 'can I have different values per branch' -> no, one set of values per project, we might add environments later, not planned yet. 'does it support .env.local' -> no, only .env in the folder that has .envsync.json.

ci: in CI use envsync pull --ci. it never prompts, and it fails with exit code 5 if .envsync.json is missing. CI tokens are read-only, so a push from CI always fails with code 2, that is on purpose. the tool honors HTTPS_PROXY if your runners sit behind a proxy.

safety stuff people should know: pull writes .env with file mode 600 so other users on the machine can't read it. pull --force saves the old file as .env.bak before it overwrites. the server keeps the last 20 versions of the values for each project. envsync history lists them and envsync restore <version> puts one back (restore is a push, so the same warning applies, it overwrites what is there now).

update with npm update -g envsync-cli. the tool prints a notice when a newer version exists, it does not update itself.

more internal noise: perf, we cache the project id in /tmp for an hour, nobody cares. the CEO demoed it at the all-hands in may and it crashed, we fixed that (it was the proxy). someone asked for a GUI, no.

history nobody cares about: v1 was bash, v2 typescript, v2.3 added diff, v2.5 added dry-run, v3 dropped the rc file. the original author left the company. the name was almost 'dotsync'.
